themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in an all stock deal valued at $115 billion including debt: 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, leaving Lumentum holders about 33% of the company. Marvell expects more than $1 billion of yearly cost savings and higher earnings in the first year after closing (company release via CNBC, Nov 2). On Oct 30 closes the offer is worth about 883.80 a Lumentum share, 5.1% above LITE's 840.70 (my calculation, Massive). Before the open MRVL traded at 192.16, down 2.16%, and LITE about 4% lower (CNBC). Separately, Oracle sold $10 billion of new stock and was down more than 2.5% premarket, and Kioxia fell about 14% after saying flash memory price gains slowed to the mid 20% range in July to September from 70% the quarter before (CNBC).
themes.for_you: No buy or put in MRVL (Wait, under its 218.02 zone floor) or LITE, which now trades as a buyout target tied to MRVL's price. Oracle selling stock to fund AI is the same cash strain that sank the spenders last week. LITE is left out of both lists: the premium is small and moves with MRVL. MU is left out: Kioxia's warning is about flash memory, not the HBM that drives MU.

innovations.name: Communications
innovations.what: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for $115 billion in stock, combining Marvell's electrical chips with Lumentum's lasers and optics for AI data centers. Marvell says the deal lifts its addressable market to $550 billion (company release via CNBC, Nov 2). It is the largest bet yet that optical links become the chokepoint inside AI clusters.
innovations.for_you: No action today. MRVL holders pay with dilution and the stock is Wait under its zone. COHR is the main independent laser maker left; a buyer paying $115 billion puts a value on its kind of asset. CIEN is left out: it is a customer and a rival. No puts in any of these before the price settles.

innovations.name: Transportation
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Aurora's Q3 letter (Oct 28) moved its 200 driverless truck goal from the end of 2026 to the end of February 2027 and set a new goal of more than 1,000 trucks by the end of 2027. Q3 revenue was $3 million, the net loss $234 million, and it had about $1.03 billion of cash and short term investments with about $250 million of cash use expected in Q4. It has passed 500,000 commercial driverless miles. No paying air taxi passenger, no final FAA drone rule and no Tesla Dallas launch were confirmed as of Nov 2.
innovations.for_you: No action. A two month slip on the truck count is small, but at about $250 million of cash use a quarter Aurora has roughly a year of runway before it needs more money. AUR has no verdict and KDK is Wait; neither is a swing or put name. KDK is left out of both lists: the news is about Aurora.

countries.name: China
countries.what: Mainland stocks rose Monday after reports that Chinese regulators will meet banks and brokers to discuss steps to support the stock market: the CSI 300 rose 0.79% and the Shanghai Composite 1.08% to 3,638.03; Hong Kong's Hang Seng was up 0.42% (CNBC, Nov 2). It came a day after the official factory index fell to 49.3.
countries.for_you: No action. Market support talk can lift Chinese stocks for days, but it does not fix weak demand; BABA and PDD stay off the buy lists and are left out here for that reason.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: Oil fell about 6% Monday morning: Brent for January was $106.54 and WTI $97.65 at 8:55am ET, after reports that Iran's supreme leader gave the government some authority to hold peace talks, Rubio said Trump would 'prefer to do it peacefully', and Iranian officials said a deal is still possible after the Qatar mediated talks (CNBC, Al Jazeera). The Wall Street Journal and New York Times still report the US is preparing for possible strikes after the Nov 3 vote (via CNBC).
countries.for_you: Swing: for the XOM, CVX, COP and EOG swing plans at or near target, a 6% oil drop is the reason to take profits or raise the stop to the entry today. Airlines get relief, but DAL is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' and UAL is Avoid; no buy. The strike risk after Tuesday is not gone.

countries.name: Japan
countries.what: Kioxia fell about 14% after warning that flash memory price gains are stalling: average NAND selling prices rose in the mid 20% range in July to September, against 70% the quarter before, and its quarterly profit guide of 2 trillion yen was below the 2.35 trillion analysts expected (CNBC, Nov 2). The Nikkei slipped 0.33% to 63,081.86.
countries.for_you: No action. Slower flash price gains are a warning for SNDK and WDC, which are not on the buy lists. MU makes mostly DRAM and HBM, so it is less exposed.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The KOSPI rose 2.24% to 5,859.08 on Nov 2, recovering part of Friday's 3.48% drop after opening 1.39% lower, as US futures and chip stocks bounced (CNBC table; CNBC's text said 2.38%, but the index points give 2.24%).
countries.for_you: No action. One up day does not end foreign selling; wait for a calm week before any Korea or memory trade. SKHY is left out: no company news.
